hints: Look carefully at Fig. 6.1 around days 10 to 12 - which hormone reaches a sharp peak just before LH shoots up?
walkthrough:
Read the Graph in Order**
Look at the solid oestrogen curve. It rises steeply from about day 8 and peaks at about 8 arbitrary units on day 11 to 12, just before the LH peak.

Link High Oestrogen to the LH Surge**
When oestrogen from the developing follicle rises above a threshold level it switches to stimulating the pituitary to release a lot of LH. That LH surge around day 12 to 13 then triggers ovulation.
Final answer: High concentration of oestrogen stimulates a surge in LH secretion, which causes ovulation.

hints: Follow the dashed progesterone curve after day 20 to day 26 - what happens to its concentration, and what would have to stay high to maintain a pregnancy?
walkthrough:
Follow Progesterone to the End of the Cycle**
Progesterone rises after ovulation to about 7 units around day 20 to 23 because the corpus luteum secretes it to maintain the endometrium.

Why a Fall Means No Pregnancy**
If fertilisation had occurred, the corpus luteum would be maintained and progesterone would stay high. Here progesterone falls to near zero by day 26, so the endometrium breaks down and menstruation occurs.
Final answer: Progesterone concentration falls sharply towards the end of the cycle (days 24-26).

hints: Start with where in the brain these pill hormones act to control the natural cycle - which gland releases FSH and LH?
If blood already contains a lot of oestrogen and progesterone from the pill, what feedback message does that send about releasing more FSH and LH?
If FSH stays low and there is no LH surge, what happens to follicle development and release of an egg?
Think beyond ovulation - how else do these hormones make fertilisation and implantation harder at the cervix and uterus?
walkthrough:
Tricking the Pituitary with Negative Feedback**
The pill keeps oestrogen and progesterone artificially high. The anterior pituitary detects this and, by negative feedback, reduces its secretion of gonadotrophins. Think of it as the body being told it is already in the luteal phase or pregnant, so no more stimulation is needed.

No FSH Means No Follicle, No LH Means No Ovulation**
With FSH inhibited, a dominant Graafian follicle does not develop and does not secrete its own oestrogen. With LH inhibited, there is no LH surge around day 12, so the follicle wall does not rupture and ovulation is prevented. This is the main contraceptive effect.

Backup Defences at Cervix and Uterus**
Progesterone also thickens cervical mucus so sperm cannot swim through easily, and prevents thickening of the endometrium so even if fertilisation occurred, implantation would be unlikely.

Final answer: Oestrogen and progesterone act on the anterior pituitary by negative feedback to inhibit secretion of FSH and LH. Without FSH the Graafian follicle does not develop and without the LH surge ovulation is prevented. Cervical mucus thickens to block sperm and the endometrium remains thin to prevent implantation.

hints: Think about what you saw in Fig. 6.1 when progesterone fell at the end of the cycle - what would stopping the pill for 7 days copy?
walkthrough:
Why a 7-Day Break**
Taking the pill for 21 days then stopping for 7 days causes a sudden fall in oestrogen and progesterone, just like the fall in progesterone at days 24 to 26 in Fig. 6.1. Without hormonal support the endometrium breaks down, so a withdrawal bleed like menstruation occurs.
Final answer: To allow withdrawal of hormones so menstruation / withdrawal bleed occurs, mimicking the natural cycle.

hints: Compare having to remember a tablet every single day with a device that works for three years - what is the main human error with the pill?
walkthrough:
Removing Daily Error**
The pill only works if taken consistently and on time - a missed pill can allow FSH, follicle development and ovulation. An implant releases hormones continuously into the blood for up to three years, giving a steady concentration with no daily action and no daily peaks and troughs.
Final answer: No need to remember to take a pill every day, so more reliable / maintains a steady hormone concentration.
